source.geographicSourceOfData: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA
source.locationDataGenerated: 250 sensor nodes distributed across San Francisco, Oakland, and San Jose metropolitan area

provenance.dataGenerationMethod: Real-time IoT sensor measurements from PurpleAir PA-II-SD sensors measuring PM2.5, PM10, temperature, humidity. Sensors transmit readings every 60 seconds via 4G/LTE to MQTT broker. Each sensor GPS-calibrated for location accuracy ±5 meters.
provenance.dataFormat: JSON stream via MQTT, schema: {timestamp: ISO8601, sensor_id: UUID, location: {lat: float, lon: float}, pm25: float (μg/m³), pm10: float (μg/m³), temperature: float (°C), humidity: float (%), battery: float (V)}
provenance.dataSubjectivity: Objective - direct physical measurements. However, PM readings affected by sensor placement (e.g., near roads vs. parks), calibration drift over time, and environmental interference (rain, fog)

qualityIndicators.calibrationFrequency: Quarterly calibration against EPA reference monitors
qualityIndicators.spatialCoverage: Average 0.8km between sensors in urban core, 2.5km in suburban areas
qualityIndicators.measurementAccuracy: ±10% for PM2.5, ±15% for PM10 compared to EPA reference monitors
qualityIndicators.dataGaps: 2.7% missing data due to sensor maintenance, network outages, and battery failures

dataProcessingSteps: Raw sensor readings ingested via MQTT broker
Outlier detection: reject readings outside 3 sigma from 24-hour rolling mean
Calibration correction: apply linear correction factors from quarterly EPA reference comparisons
Geofencing: reject readings with GPS accuracy > 50 meters
Battery-level filtering: mark readings with battery < 3.2V as low-quality
Data aggregation: hourly averages computed for public dashboard

use.intendedUse: Public health monitoring, air quality forecasting models, environmental policy analysis, academic research on urban air pollution patterns. Data powers public air quality dashboard and mobile apps for residents.
use.restrictions: Public domain for non-commercial and research use. Commercial use (e.g., real estate analytics, targeted advertising) requires licensing agreement. Cannot be used to identify individual residents or infer private behavior patterns.
use.legalRightsToUse: Data collected with city government authorization. Sensor placements on public property and consenting private property. Complies with California IoT Privacy Law (SB-327). No personal data collected.
use.privacyMeasures: Sensors located only in public spaces or with explicit property owner consent. Precise GPS coordinates (±5m) not publicly disclosed - published maps use 100m grid aggregation to prevent address-level identification. No camera or audio sensors. Data retention: raw data 90 days, aggregated data indefinite.
use.dataProcessingLocation: Data ingestion: AWS us-west-1. Real-time processing: Kafka clusters in us-west-1. Long-term storage: S3 buckets in us-west-1 with cross-region replication to us-east-1. All data remains within US borders per municipal data governance policy.

_comments.why_this_matters: IoT sensor data raises location privacy concerns even without personal identifiers. Must document spatial precision, retention policies, and processing locations for GDPR/CCPA compliance.
_comments.key_challenges: Sensor calibration drift over time, handling missing data from network outages, balancing spatial precision with privacy protection, managing data volume (250 sensors × 60 readings/hour × 24 hours = 360K records/day)
_comments.real_world_use: Similar to PurpleAir network data used by EPA, academic researchers, and air quality apps like AirNow. Provenance documentation enables data sharing with research institutions while maintaining privacy commitments to residents.
